summary: Michigan's 1892 brick tower at the Straits of Mackinac, joined to its keepers' house; fog signal 1890, light first lit 1892, discontinued 1957 when the Mackinac Bridge opened.

structures.note: 50 ft to the focal plane per the Board (1892); 45 ft to the gallery; 13 ft 4 in outside diameter; limestone ashlar base; attached to keepers' dwelling
frame fog-signal house 22 by 40 ft (1892 description); a new brick fog-signal building was built in 1906 and in operation in 1907

access.note: Operated by Mackinac State Historic Parks; visitors can climb the tower (LighthouseFriends, 2007 figures).

facts.agency: Mackinac State Historic Parks (Mackinac Island State Park Commission from 1960)

events.note: Fog signal first operated 5 November 1890; the light did not yet exist
Tower and keepers' dwellings contracted March 1892; erection begun late May 1892
Fourth-order Fresnel lens (Sautter, Lemonier & Co.) in the lantern
Lit for the first time on the night of 25 October 1892 (Board report for fiscal 1893); the Board's list of new lights gives 26 October
Additional land needed for the fog signal, which was to move fifty feet east; condemnation begun
New brick fog-signal building in operation
Signal changed from flashing red to flashing white (LighthouseFriends; not yet found in a primary source)
Discontinued after the Mackinac Bridge was completed
Purchased by the Mackinac Island State Park Commission and added to the state park
Closed for budget and attendance reasons
Reopened as a restoration in progress

corrections.why: 1890 is the fog signal's first operation (5 Nov 1890). The light was first lit on 25 October 1892 (Board report for fiscal 1893; LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: The station record gives Emmet County; the USLHS place record gives Cheboygan County. Not resolved from the sources read; a human should check a county source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Board's report for fiscal 1893 gives the night of 25 October 1892 for the first lighting and a completion date of 27 October; the Board's list of new lights gives 26 October 1892 for the same light. The story uses 25 October.
USLHS and LighthouseFriends give 1957 (after the Mackinac Bridge). A Michigan marker text quoted on a secondary website says 1958; not checked against a primary source.
The USLHS roster runs Campbell's head-keeper stint to 1958; LighthouseFriends says he was in charge until 1957. Both are given in the story.

notes_for_editor: Board-report citations: scan pages 16, 166, 170, 489, 492, 493 are read from the corpus OCR page index. The printed page numbers for those scans are marked '?' by the corpus tool (unconfirmed), so the footnotes give scan pages only; check the image before printing 'p. N'. The Commissioner's 1915 p. 64 (scan 69) is confirmed on the page's OCR head. The fiscal 1895, 1896 and 1900 Board volumes have no page index in the corpus, so those footnotes give the volume and entry, not a page; the 1895 'some 600 hours' and 1896 fog-signal entries are cited to the volume. The 1915 table row naming W. Barnum was checked on the page image (scan 69, printed p. 64): it names J. M. Marshall and J. H. Sullivan (White Shoal) with Barnum, the vessel column reads Launch Ida L., and the nature column reads Saved launch during gale. The story now states that credit. The 1913 signal change and 1929 electrification come from LighthouseFriends only; no official source read confirms them (the corpus has no 1913 Commissioner volume). NRHP nomination 69000068: the NPGallery PDF returned no text and the NARA catalog is out of bounds, so it was not read. Wikipedia not used. Chronicling America (Michigan papers, 1890-1957, 'Mackinac Point' 'lighthouse') returned one 1941 Ypsilanti page, not read. County conflict unresolved (see corrections). The archive roster line for Campbell runs to 1958, LighthouseFriends to 1957.
